mcat_description.short: FRP Cabin is a prefabricated, portable structure made from Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP/GRP) panels, sold as a complete ready-to-install unit primarily used as security guard rooms, site offices, and portable workspaces.
mcat_description.long: FRP Cabins are factory-built portable enclosures constructed using fibre reinforced plastic (FRP or GRP) panels mounted on a mild steel base frame, offering a lightweight, corrosion-resistant, and weather-proof alternative to conventional brick-and-mortar construction. In the Indian B2B market, they are predominantly supplied as security/guard cabins, portable office cabins, site supervisor rooms, check post cabins, and changing rooms, with standard sizes ranging from 4x4 ft to 20x10 ft and customisation available for dimensions, colour, roofing style (pyramid, gable, flat), and electrical fittings. Key material properties include UV resistance, electrical insulation, termite-proof construction, and low maintenance, making them suitable for outdoor deployment at construction sites, industrial estates, residential complexes, and toll plazas. They are sold per piece for standard sizes and per sq ft for larger custom configurations, with Pune, Ahmedabad, Faridabad, and Chennai being the dominant manufacturing hubs in India.

market_context: FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic) cabins are a well-established product category in the Indian prefabricated structures market, with Pune, Ahmedabad, Faridabad, and Chennai as the primary manufacturing hubs. The dominant commercial form is the security/guard cabin, available in standard sizes from 4x4 ft to 10x10 ft, with larger custom office and site cabins available up to 20x10 ft. Key material differentiators versus MS/steel cabins include corrosion resistance, UV protection, electrical insulation, termite-proof construction, and lighter weight enabling easier relocation. GRP (Glass Reinforced Plastic) is used interchangeably with FRP in the Indian market — both terms refer to the same product. Buyers evaluate primarily on size/dimensions, wall panel thickness (5mm single-skin to 50mm insulated sandwich), roof style (pyramid, gable, flat), colour, and included electrical fittings. The category also attracts toilet/bathroom cabin enquiries (FRP Portable Toilet is a sibling MCAT) and portable home/habitation enquiries — these are routing contamination signals. No BIS/IS standard specific to FRP cabins was found in available sources (single source — low confidence); cabins using IS-grade steel structural components are referenced by manufacturers. The market is highly fragmented with no dominant national brand; buyers typically source from regional manufacturers and evaluate on specification and customisation capability.
